newsitem.title: USA: High Plains Wheat - Dealers busy as harvest expands.
newsitem.headline: High Plains Wheat - Dealers busy as harvest expands.

text.p: Grain dealers in the High Plains were busy buying hard red winter wheat Tuesday morning as harvest expanded in Texas and Oklahoma.

"I've heard varying reports on the Oklahoma crop but overall it's coming out pretty good in terms of yields -- better than people expected," a south central Kansas dealer said. "I think most of Kansas will also be pleasantly surprised."
Wheat harvest was also just getting started in southern Kansas, according to the weekly crop progress report from Kansas' Department of Agricultural Statistics.
There were reports of hail damage to wheat Monday night in northern Oklahoma and southern Kansas, but dealers said they did not know how bad the overall damage was.
"I don't know how much damage there was across the whole state," an Oklahoma dealer said. "But one farmer up in Medford said he lost 300 acres of wheat to golf ball-sized hail."
Meanwhile, basis bids were steady to weaker Tuesday on harvest pressure.
Basis values in cents/bu against KCBT wheat, cash=dollars/bu.
